content: 1. Mortality Outcomes (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): In the study by Abd-Elsalam (2021), 4 deaths occurred in the ivermectin group compared to 3 in the control group. Chaccour (2021) reported no deaths in either group. López-Medina (2021) observed 1 death in the ivermectin group and none in the control group. Ravikirti (2021) reported 4 deaths in the ivermectin group and none in the control group. Vallejos (2021) recorded 3 deaths in the ivermectin group and 4 in the control group. The overall risk ratio for mortality in mild to moderate cases was 0.72 (95% CI: 0.28 to 1.85), with no significant difference between ivermectin and control (P = 0.50). 2. Mortality Outcomes (Severe COVID-19): In the study by Okumuş (2021), 6 deaths were reported in both the ivermectin and control groups. The risk ratio for severe cases was 0.67 (95% CI: 0.27 to 1.64), with no significant difference (P = 0.38). 3. Need for Mechanical Ventilation (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): Abd-Elsalam (2021) reported 3 events in both the ivermectin and control groups. Ravikirti (2021) observed 5 events in the ivermectin group and 1 in the control group. Vallejos (2021) recorded 3 events in the ivermectin group and 4 in the control group. The overall risk ratio was 0.81 (95% CI: 0.30 to 2.19), with no significant difference (P = 0.67). 4. Clinical Improvement (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): López-Medina (2021) reported clinical improvement in 164 out of 200 patients in the ivermectin group and 156 out of 198 in the control group. The risk ratio was 1.04 (95% CI: 0.94 to 1.15), with no significant difference (P = 0.42). 5. Clinical Improvement (Severe COVID-19): Okumuş (2021) observed clinical improvement in 22 out of 30 patients in the ivermectin group and 16 out of 30 in the control group. The risk ratio was 1.38 (95% CI: 0.92 to 2.05), with no significant difference (P = 0.12). 6. Serious Adverse Events (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): Ahmed (2021), Chaccour (2021), López-Medina (2021), Ravikirti (2021), and Vallejos (2021) collectively reported 2 serious adverse events in the ivermectin group and none in the control group. The risk ratio was not estimable due to the low number of events. 7. Serious Adverse Events (Severe COVID-19): Okumuş (2021) reported no serious adverse events in either group. 8. Hospitalization (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): Samaha (2021) reported 3 hospitalizations in the ivermectin group and none in the control group. Vallejos (2021) observed 21 hospitalizations in the ivermectin group and 14 in the control group. The overall risk ratio was 0.67 (95% CI: 0.35 to 1.29), with no significant difference (P = 0.31). 9. Duration of Hospitalization (Mild to Moderate COVID-19): Abd-Elsalam (2021) reported a mean duration of 10.97 days in the ivermectin group and 8.82 days in the control group. Ahmed (2021) observed a mean duration of 9.7 days in the ivermectin group and 9.6 days in the control group. Shahbaznejad (2021) reported a mean duration of 8.4 days in the ivermectin group and 7.1 days in the control group. The overall mean difference was -1.32 days (95% CI: -1.57 to -1.06), favoring ivermectin (P < 0.00001). 10. Risk of Bias Assessment: Random sequence generation (selection bias) was adequately addressed in most studies. Allocation concealment was generally well-implemented, though some studies had unclear methods. Blinding of participants and personnel was variable, with some studies showing high risk of performance bias. Outcome assessment blinding was generally adequate. Incomplete outcome data and selective reporting were minimal in most studies. These findings suggest that ivermectin does not significantly reduce mortality, the need for mechanical ventilation, or hospitalization in COVID-19 patients. While there may be a slight reduction in hospitalization duration, the clinical significance of this finding is uncertain.
